The clinical summary presents a patient with long-standing, non-inflammatory knee pain attributed to osteoarthritis — but the dominant, urgent finding is profound leukocytosis (58,000/mm³) driven almost entirely by lymphocytosis (absolute lymphocyte count = 50,000/mm³). This degree of isolated, sustained lymphocytosis in an adult is highly atypical for reactive causes (e.g., viral infection, autoimmune disease, or stress lymphocytosis), which rarely exceed 20,000/mm³ and are usually transient. The summary explicitly states this pattern is “highly suggestive of a clonal B-cell lymphoproliferative disorder”, and the ordered flow cytometry panel (CD5, CD19, CD20, CD23, kappa/lambda) is the gold-standard test to confirm clonality and immunophenotype — precisely aligned with diagnostic criteria for chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) or monoclonal B-cell lymphocytosis (MBL). Chronic lymphocytic leukemia
